3D density surfaces

Source: R/stat-isodensity-3d.R
geom_isodensity_3d.Rd

Estimates the density of a 3D point cloud, and draws surfaces of constant density enclosing given fractions of it: the 3D analog of ggplot2::geom_density_2d(). Each surface bounds the smallest region containing a given fraction of the estimated probability mass (a "highest density region"), so that e.g. probs = 0.5 shows where the densest half of the data lie.

Usage

geom_isodensity_3d(
  mapping = NULL,
  data = NULL,
  stat = StatIsodensity3D,
  position = "identity",
  ...,
  probs = 0.5,
  n = 30,
  h = NULL,
  adjust = 1,
  cap = FALSE,
  light = NULL,
  cull_backfaces = FALSE,
  scale_depth = TRUE,
  na.rm = FALSE,
  show.legend = NA,
  inherit.aes = TRUE
)

stat_isodensity_3d(
  mapping = NULL,
  data = NULL,
  geom = GeomIsosurface3D,
  position = "identity",
  ...,
  probs = 0.5,
  n = 30,
  h = NULL,
  adjust = 1,
  cap = FALSE,
  light = NULL,
  cull_backfaces = FALSE,
  scale_depth = TRUE,
  na.rm = FALSE,
  show.legend = NA,
  inherit.aes = TRUE
)

Arguments

mapping

Set of aesthetic mappings created by aes().

data

The data to be displayed in this layer: a grid of points, with one row for every combination of x, y, and z values, such as produced by expand.grid(). Even grid spacing is not required.

stat

The statistical transformation to use on the data. Defaults to StatIsosurface3D.

position

Position adjustment, defaults to "identity". To collapse the result onto one 2D surface, use position_on_face().

...

Other arguments passed on to the layer function (typically GeomPolygon3D), such as aesthetics like colour, fill, linewidth, etc.

probs

Numeric vector of fractions of probability mass, between 0 and 1, for each surface to enclose. Defaults to 0.5, a single surface around the densest half of the data. Nested surfaces hide one another unless they are translucent, e.g. with alpha.

n

Number of grid points along each axis at which the density is estimated. Larger values give smoother surfaces, at a cost in time that grows with its cube.

h

Bandwidths of the kernel: a single number, or one for each of x, y, and z. As in stat_density_3d() and MASS::kde2d(), a bandwidth is four times the standard deviation of the Gaussian kernel. If NULL (the default), each is estimated with the normal reference rule for three dimensions, 4 * (4/5)^(1/7) * s * n^(-1/7), where n is the number of points and s the smaller of their standard deviation and interquartile range divided by 1.34. Weights are ignored in estimating bandwidths.

adjust

Multiplier for the bandwidths, a single number or one per axis, e.g. adjust = 2 for a smoother estimate.

cap

Logical indicating whether to close surfaces with flat caps where they're cut by limits set on the plot's scales, so that they show solid cross sections rather than being left open there. Defaults to FALSE.

light

A lighting specification object created by light(), light("none") or the string "none" to disable lighting, or NULL to inherit plot-level lighting. Set plot-level lighting by adding light() to the plot, and layer-specific lighting via the light argument of geom_*_3d() functions, which takes precedence.

cull_backfaces

Logical indicating whether to remove triangles that face away from the viewer. Surfaces face outward from the regions they enclose, so for opaque surfaces that close on themselves, TRUE removes only hidden triangles and speeds up rendering. Defaults to FALSE, since surfaces that are translucent or cut open by the edge of the grid show their inner side.

scale_depth

Controls whether polygon linewidths are scaled to make closer lines wider and farther lines narrower, based on the mean depth of a polygon. TRUE (the default) applies full scaling and FALSE disables it; a number sets the strength directly, where 1 matches TRUE, 0 matches FALSE, values below 1 subdue the effect and values above 1 exaggerate it. This affects the layer only; use coord_3d(scale_depth = ) for gridlines, cube borders, axis ticks, and axis text.

na.rm

If FALSE, missing values are removed.

show.legend

Logical indicating whether this layer should be included in legends.

inherit.aes

If FALSE, overrides the default aesthetics.

geom

The geometric object used to display the data. Defaults to GeomIsosurface3D, a variant of geom_polygon_3d().

Value

A Layer object that can be added to a ggplot.

Details

The density is a Gaussian kernel density estimate, evaluated on a grid that extends beyond the data far enough for surfaces to close, and surfaces are triangulated with the marching cubes algorithm. Where limits are set on the plot's scales, e.g. with ggplot2::xlim() or zlim(), points outside them are removed before the density is estimated, as elsewhere in ggplot2, and surfaces are cut at them, leaving them open there unless cap = TRUE. Cutting doesn't change the fractions of mass the surfaces enclose, which refer to the whole estimate.

Aesthetics

stat_isodensity_3d() requires the following aesthetics:

  • x, y, z: Point coordinates

and understands weight, giving points' relative weights in the density. Grouping aesthetics give a separate density for each group.

geom_isodensity_3d() draws surfaces like geom_isosurface_3d(), and understands the same aesthetics.

Computed variables

  • prob: The fraction of probability mass the surface encloses

  • level: The density on the surface

  • normal_x, normal_y, normal_z: Components of each triangle's unit normal, pointing outward from the region the surface encloses

  • cap: Whether a triangle is part of a cap (see cap)

Dependencies

Surfaces are computed with the rmarchingcubes package, which must be installed.

See also

geom_isosurface_3d() and geom_isofunction_3d() for isosurfaces of gridded fields and of functions, geom_hull_3d() for hulls of point clouds, stat_density_3d() for 2D densities drawn as surfaces.

Examples

# The densest half of each species
ggplot(iris, aes(Sepal.Length, Sepal.Width, Petal.Length, fill = Species)) +
  geom_isodensity_3d() +
  light(mode = "hsl", direction = c(-1, 1, 0)) +
  coord_3d()


# Nested translucent surfaces around Fiji earthquakes, which trace
# the Tonga slab subducting beneath the Pacific plate
# \donttest{
ggplot(quakes, aes(long, lat, -depth)) +
  geom_isodensity_3d(alpha = .5, aes(fill = after_stat(prob)),
                     probs = c(0.25, 0.5, 0.75)) +
  geom_point_3d(size = 0.2) +
  scale_fill_viridis_c() +
  coord_3d(yaw = 180, roll = -70, scales = "fixed", ratio = c(1, 1, .01)) +
  labs(z = "depth (km)") +
  light(direction = c(-1, 1, 1)) +
  zlim(NA, 0) +
  theme_dark() + theme(panel.border = element_rect(color = "gray70"))

# }
